Charity Spotlight: Lead to Read KC

By
Sarah McGinnity
-
August 12, 2026
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
ReddIt
Email
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:56
    Instaread

    Kansas City Mom Collective is featuring an organization each month that supports Kansas City families. We hope to introduce you to a new organization and provide ways you can support their mission. To nominate an organization to be featured here, email us.

    Lead to Read KC mobilizes the community to solve the literacy crisis by connecting students with Reading Mentors, resources and unwavering support. Lead to Read KC serves children in the KC metro by providing Reading Mentors through our 33 partner schools, school tutoring support via our partnership with Hoot Reading, engagement with local children’s book authors and increased book access through 88 free Reading is Everywhere book distribution baskets.

    The Story of Lead to Read

    Lead to Read KC was founded in 2011 by two former teachers, Lynn and Jean Rundle, who were passionate about helping children succeed. After years of mentoring and tutoring teens who struggled in school, they realized the problem wasn’t just that the kids weren’t reading; it was that reading didn’t seem relevant to them.

    With this in mind, they set out to create a program that would not only improve reading skills but also instill a love of reading. After months of research and consultation with leaders in education and the local community, Lynn and Jean launched what is now known as the Reading Mentoring program.

    The initiative began with just a handful of volunteers in several Kansas City-area schools and has since flourished to include 2,075 Reading Mentors. Children who read proficiently by third grade will be more successful in school and life. Students with a Lead to Read KC Reading Mentor grow more in their reading skills and enjoyment of reading than their peers in the same school.

    We are most proud of our ability to mobilize the community to solve the literacy crisis. From individuals who plan and execute book drives to volunteers who show up weekly to read with students, we know that every Kansas Citian can play a part in making Kansas City a literate city.

    How Lead to Read Helps

    “My daughter’s interest and enjoyment in reading increased noticeably once she started with Lead to Read KC. She looks forward to it every week, and her reading scores have improved a lot!” Laura W., Lead to Read KC school parent

    “Today I announced to the students that their reading buddies were coming, and there was an instantaneous cheer! Most of the students don’t have people who sit on the sofa with them and read. When the reading buddies come in, they get to see adults who are off their phones and focused on them.” Kari Bowles, Garfield Elementary

    “If you take a lunch hour every day, you can give up one a week to help a student develop a life-changing skill. And the reward? It’s huge. You’ll see growth, you’ll build trust, and for 30 minutes each week, the world just slows down. I plan to be a Reading Mentor for the rest of my life.” Alane Watts, Reading Mentor

    “In a busy world, Lead to Read gives you a chance to slow down and remember what is important. If you dedicate time to volunteer for Lead to Read, it will be the highlight of your week.” Shenee Davis-Cross, Reading Mentor

    “It’s hard to convey what a blessing the books are to the children who come to One City Cafe. They don’t have much materially, and it brings amazing smiles to their faces when they choose a book to keep!” Jackie O’Brien, One City Cafe volunteer.

    How KC Parents Can Help

    Volunteer as a Mentor

    Adults 18 and older can volunteer to become Reading Mentors at one of our 33 partner schools. Mentors read with the same student weekly or twice monthly during 30-minute sessions coordinated by Lead to Read staff and partner schools. Learn more and apply at leadtoreadkc.org/volunteer. Questions? Contact volunteer@leadtoreadkc.org.

    Volunteer as a Family

    Families can sign-up to sort and process book donations and pack books for delivery at either Fun Fridays or Fourth Thursday Fulfillment. Learn more and sign-up on our website, leadtoreadkc.org, under the events tab.

    Donate Books

    Families can also support our work by participating in our first ever Kansas City Book Drive, August 17-23. Donate new or like-new children’s books at your favorite independent bookstore location. Find participating bookstores.

    Have books to donate after our city-wide book drive? Contact Linda Hughes to arrange a drop-off.

    Lead to Read can be found on Facebook and Instagram.

      Sarah McGinnity
      Sarah grew up in Manhattan, Kansas (Go Cats!), she moved to Minnesota where she met her husband, Shea. Realizing how much she hated snow in May, she convinced him to move to Kansas City in 2010. Together they have lived in Midtown, Waldo, the Plaza, and now Overland Park. Sarah is mom to four kids including a teenager and a toddler. She has her master’s in urban administration and is passionate about making Kansas City a more equitable and supportive community. In between the crazy, she likes to drink coffee, run, hike, travel as much as possible, and experience all things Kansas City!
